title: Manus Pricing 2026: Plans, Credits & What Tasks Cost
summary: Manus pricing tiers start at $20 monthly for 4,000 credits, with a $40 option for 8,000. Determine your credit needs to select the right plan.
body_markdown:
## Activepieces for repeat steps Manus credits shouldn't buy


The Monday report is the kind of step that shouldn't draw on agent credits at all, and Activepieces never meters how many flows you build: the public pricing page lists unlimited flows from Free through Ultimate, and the only meter is credits per run, at 1 credit however many steps the run has.


Zapier bills a task per action and Make a credit per module, so there the tidy design, with fetching, formatting and the low-credit alert as separate small workflows, costs more each time it runs.


On Activepieces, splitting a fragile mega-automation into ten small flows adds nothing to the bill for existing.


[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) runs that Monday sequence on a trigger: you define the steps once, and it executes them the same way each time without re-deciding anything, with unlimited flows on the Free plan's 1,000 credits a month.


### Separating fixed workflow steps from Manus agent work


Take a weekly report: pull last week's numbers, format them into a summary, post it to a team channel. Nothing in that sequence changes between runs.


Asking Manus to do it each Monday means paying for planning and tool selection that produce the same answer as the week before.


The cost per run is small, but it recurs, and a recurring cost with no variation's exactly what a fixed workflow exists to remove.


According to Activepieces, a flow is a trigger followed by a chain of steps, and it has a schedule trigger for time-based runs.


The flow below has four boxes in a line: scheduled trigger, pull data, format, send message. A branch off the line leads to a low-credit alert.


Beside it sits a separate Manus agent box, marked open-ended research. Read it as a dividing line: everything in the left-to-right chain's predictable and cheap to repeat, while the agent box's where the outcome depends on judgment.


That split's why this complements Manus rather than replacing it. A workflow cannot decide which sources matter for a question nobody has asked yet. An agent can. Put the agent on the open-ended work and keep it off the Monday report.


### Manus credit alerts and spend approval


Tie the branch in that flow back to a spending rule.


A workflow can check a condition and route to a different step, so a low-credit warning can go to whoever owns the budget instead of surfacing mid-task, on your heaviest day, when the balance's already gone.


Pausing a flow to wait for a person to approve before it continues is covered in Activepieces's documentation too. Placed ahead of any step that would start a Manus run, that gives you a checkpoint: someone confirms the task's worth the credits before they're spent.


I wouldn't claim it enforces a hard cap, because the limit itself lives in Manus's plan, not in the workflow. What it gives you's a rule you can actually point at, written into the flow rather than remembered.
